Command: Rest on the Feast of Weeks
Summary: The Feast of Weeks is kept as a holy convocation of rest, at the end of the fifty days counted from the sheaf.
Commandment: Keep the Feast of Weeks as a holy convocation and rest on it.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The rest crowned the grain harvest with worship rather than with more work. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
Function: The Feast of Weeks was kept as a holy convocation of rest, at the end of the fifty days counted from the sheaf — a ceremonial law of harvest worship. Its goal was to crown the grain harvest with worship rather than more work, the firstfruits gathered and the day given to God. It did not address a particular evil; its work was thanksgiving and remembrance, not restraint. The rest said the harvest was God's gift before it was man's labour, and the feast stopped the work to say so.
